title: At Station ALOHA, anthropogenic carbon on sigma0 26.5 rose about 4 umol/kg less than steady ventilation gives (1988-2024); this agrees with slower ventilation, not faster respiration
abstract: Question: campaign work explains the North Pacific O2 loss on sigma0 26.5 by slower ventilation after the winter outcrop shrank, but O2 alone cannot separate slower ventilation from faster respiration. Approach: anthropogenic carbon (Cant) is a transient tracer whose source still increases, so older water holds less Cant than transient steady state (TSS) gives. Faster respiration gives no Cant deficit. We calculated the C* carbon index X from bottle DIC, alkalinity and O2 on density classes at Station ALOHA (HOT, 1988-2024) and BATS (1991-2025). We hashed the plan and the TTD predictions (CFC-12 ages from GLODAPv2.2023) before we used any carbon value. Results (sigma0 26.5, 95% intervals, umol/kg): at ALOHA, X rose 8.6 (2.8 to 14.4) and TSS gives 14.0 (8.9 to 16.6). The deficit D = -5.2 (-12.0 to +2.4) lies between the slower-ventilation predictions (-2.3 TTD stretch; -7.2 loss of young water), but the pre-registered test is not resolved because the interval contains 0. Added analyses replaced two assumed errors with data: deep-water epoch offsets at fixed potential temperature (DIC -0.3, TA +1.5, O2 +0.5) and CFC-consistent TTD pairs. They give D = -4.4 (-8.5 to -0.8), P(D<0) = 0.99, close to the young-water-loss prediction. Light control classes (25.8-26.2), where AOU changed little, give D = -0.4 to -0.8, all intervals contain 0. Class slope and time-shape tests agree in sign, but each is inconclusive alone. BATS gives a formal 'ventilation supported' result (D -9.2), but we do not accept it: carbon samples before 1998 almost never reach 26.5, and the BATS deficit does not follow AOU. A phosphate-based index is biased on the control classes. Limitations: the supporting estimate is post hoc; it assumes constant deep-water chemistry, constant air-sea CO2 disequilibrium and C:O ratio; one site. Implication: the ALOHA carbon data agree with the ventilation explanation and exclude respiration-only change at about the 99% level under the added constraints. The O2 loss came with an about 11% smaller Cant gain on this layer.
